chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about so-and-so — his worship, his religiosity, and his virtue. So he said: 'How is his intellect?' I said: 'I do not know.' So he said: 'Indeed, the reward is according to the measure of the intellect.'

Indeed, a man from the Children of Israel was worshipping God on an island from the islands of the sea — green, fresh, abundant in trees, and with flowing water. And indeed an angel from the angels passed by him and said: O my Lord! Show me the reward of this servant of Yours. So God the Exalted showed him that, and the angel considered it little. So God the Exalted revealed to him to accompany him.

So the angel came to him in the form of a human being and said to him: Who are you? He said: I am a worshipping man; news of your place and your worship in this location has reached me, so I came to you to worship God with you. He was with him that day.

When morning came, the angel said to him: Your place is truly scenic and is suitable for nothing but worship. So the worshipper said to him: There is indeed a defect in this place of ours. He said: What is it? He said: There is no animal for our Lord. If He had a donkey, we would graze it in this spot, for this pasture is being wasted.

That angel said to him: And does your Lord not have a donkey? He said: If He had a donkey, such pasture as this would not be wasted. So God revealed to the angel: I reward him only according to the measure of his intellect.

key_terms.استقله: Deemed it little/insignificant — the angel's initial underestimation of the worshipper's reward
key_terms.الثواب على قدر العقل: The reward is proportioned to the intellect — the central maxim of this hadith
key_terms.عقل: Intellect, reason — the cognitive and theological faculty that gives value to worship

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between intellect and divine reward?
ai.summary: Sulayman al-Daylami narrated to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about a man distinguished by his worship and piety, to which the Imam responded with the principle that divine reward is proportioned to intellect. He then narrated the parable of an Israelite worshipper on a lush island, whose intense devotion was undermined by his ignorance — thinking God might need a donkey to avoid wasting pasture. God revealed that He rewards according to the measure of one's intellect, not mere quantity of worship. This hadith was addressed to companions of the Imam who might overvalue outward religious practice without developing sound theological understanding.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman Al Daylami, from his father who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, of so and so, and (about) his worship, and his Religion and his merits’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How is his intellect?’ I said, ‘I do not know’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Rewards are (based) upon the measurement of the intellect.

A man from the Children of Israel was worshipping Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in an island from the islands of the sea, (which was) green, scenic, there being a lot of trees, at the back of the water (lakes & rivers), and that an Angel from the Angels passed by him, so he said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Show me the Rewards of this servant of Yours<sup>azwj</sup>’. 
So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Showed him that, and the Angel considered it to be little. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Revealed unto him, that he should accompany him.

So the Angel went over to him in the image of a human being. So he (the man) said to him (the Angel), ‘Who are you?’ He said, ‘I am a worshipping man. (News) of your position and your worship reached me in this place, so I came over to you in order to worship Allah<sup>azwj</sup> along with you’. 
It was so that he was with him for that day of his.

So when it was morning, the Angel said to him: ‘Your place is scenic and it is not correct for anything except for the worship’. So the worshipper said to him, ‘There is a fault with this place of ours’. So he said to him: ‘And what is it?’ He said, ‘There is no animal of our Lord<sup>azwj</sup>. Had there been a donkey of His<sup>azwj</sup>, we would have grazed it in this place, for this pasture is being wasted’.

So that Angel said to him: ‘And there is no donkey for your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>?’ So he said, ‘Had there been a donkey for Him<sup>azwj</sup>, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not have Wasted the plush pasture like this’. 
So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto the Angel: “But rather, I<sup>azwj</sup> am Rewarding him upon the measurement of his intellect”’.
